established.method: Semantic revert instead of file revert. prove-red could not bisect this change: src/lib/pageTitle.ts is both the file carrying the fix and the module the test imports, so reverting it leaves the test unable to resolve its import — it reported did-not-build/missing, an UNKNOWN, not a negative. The paths cannot be separated, so I restored the pre-fix RULE inside the helper body instead of removing the file: composePageTitle temporarily returned the old ternary 'pageTitle ? `${pageTitle} · ${siteTitle}` : siteTitle', leaving the file, its exports and the test fixture untouched, then ran refresh-tests --test composePageTitle in both worlds.
established.evidence: With the pre-fix rule in place: 3 of 5 failed (2 passed) — 'does not append the site title when the page title already is it' (got 'The Puzzle School · The Puzzle School'), 'treats a differently-cased or padded match as the same title', and 'falls back to the site title when the page passes none' (the whitespace-only title is truthy under the old ternary, so it produced '    · The Puzzle School'). With the dedupe rule restored: 5/5 passed. The two survivors — the ordinary-page suffix case and the renamed-site case — are intentional survival guards pinning the behavior the fix must NOT change. The fix was restored immediately after the measurement and re-verified green.
